title: Paying Off a PracticePay Patient Financing Plan in One Payment
content:
A PracticePay Patient Financing plan can be paid off in full today with one payment from a linked bank account. The payoff amount is the amount a patient pays in that one payment; a payment of that amount is applied like any other payment, and any part of it that the plan's final interest posting does not use becomes a credit balance refunded under the credit balance rule.

## When a payoff amount is worked out

A payoff amount is worked out only after the plan's ledger carries the late-fee relief owed on the plan's latest late fee under the make-up relief schedules.

A payoff amount is not worked out until the plan's ledger carries the returned-payment-fee relief owed on the fee of the plan's latest returned payment.

Both sentences speak of what the plan's ledger carries: the payoff amount is not worked out while the ledger does not yet carry that relief.

A plan whose payoff amount works out to 0.00 owes nothing, and no payoff payment is taken.

## The payoff payment: `pay_off_plan_f18fb847`

**What it does.** It makes a single online ACH debit from one of the patient's linked bank accounts for the amount given. The payment is credited to the plan today toward its oldest unpaid due date, the plan balance falls by the amount paid and the amount past due is cleared; any part of the amount beyond what the plan finally owes stays on the plan as a credit balance.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `pay_off_plan_f18fb847` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to authorize the debit.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `pos_plan_id` | reference number of the PracticePay plan being paid, as returned by the PracticePay plan lookup | identifier |
| `bank_account_id` | reference number of the patient's linked bank account to debit, as returned by the linked bank account lookup | identifier |
| `payment_amount` | the amount of the one-time payment | USD, 2 decimal places, a positive amount; debited and stored rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `pos_txn_id` (reference number of the payment entry), `pos_plan_id` (the plan paid), `bank_account_id` (the account debited), `payment_amount` (the amount credited, USD with 2 decimal places), `effective_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `plan_balance` (the plan balance left after the payment, USD with 2 decimal places; a negative figure is a credit balance). A `pos_txn_id` in the receipt means the payment is credited.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A receipt reading a plan balance of 0.00 after the payment shows the plan was paid to zero; a receipt reading a negative plan balance, for example minus 3.10, shows a credit balance of 3.10 left on the plan.
